question: Do FIII-versus-FV telemetry-classified initiation odds genuinely differ across the six source projects beyond finite binomial variation, including strata with separated cells?
input: results/stage_specific_condition_gate_v1.json, exact expert-corrected project/stage counts, FIII and FV only; no condition predictor
margin_conditioning: Within each project fix n_FIII, n_FV and total observed source-classified initiators across these two stages. Sample possible FV initiating counts by Fisher's noncentral hypergeometric distribution.
null: All six projects share the same conditional log odds ratio for FV versus FIII, but have unrestricted project-specific baseline initiation odds. No stage-by-project interaction.
alternative: Each project has its own FV-vs-FIII odds ratio; boundary/separation are allowed with finite likelihood supremum.
statistic: Twice the conditional log-likelihood difference between saturated-by-project and common log-odds models.
calibration: Seed 20261008, 10000 parametric bootstrap replicates conditional on each project's stage-by-outcome margins using the fitted common odds ratio. Refit the common odds ratio in every simulated dataset; report Monte Carlo p as (1+extreme)/(B+1).
sensitivity: Report project 2x2 counts, log odds estimates/boundary, leave-one-project-out conditional common OR and heterogeneity deviance without treating asymptotic Wald intervals as reliable in separated cells.
inferential_boundary: Post-hoc after observing project reversal; this is an exploratory descriptive heterogeneity test.
Conditional-on-margins inference applies to telemetry-classified initiation labels, not true physiological departures.
Project and hydrology, cohort composition, release year, tagging design and detection opportunities remain confounded.
Failure to reject common OR does not prove no interaction; six project contexts limit power.
The test does not account for fish and observation-history misclassification or infer escapement.
